Binding an existing name to a new value

blocks.title: A saved value is not a live link
blocks.caption: Evaluate the right side using the current value, then bind the left-hand name. The saved integer does not update when count is reassigned.

blocks.title: Python 3 code
blocks.text:
count = 8
saved = count
count = count + 2
print(count)
print(saved)

The outputs are 10 and 8 on separate lines. saved = count uses the value available at that moment. It does not store a formula that keeps following count. count = count + 2 is valid assignment: read the old 8, calculate 10, then rebind count. It is not a claim that 8 equals 10.

blocks.label: After count becomes 10, add saved = count and print(saved). Predict the new output and explain why this is different from expecting saved to change automatically.

guided_practice.title: Trace a saved value
guided_practice.prompt: Trace the five-line count and saved program. Record both printed outputs, then predict the result of assigning saved = count after the change. Check with a run or label a paper trace.
guided_practice.answer: Original outputs 10 then 8. After the new assignment, saved becomes 10. Keep actual observations separate. Reading an integer value earlier does not create a live link to another name.

independent_case.title: Keep division meanings separate
independent_case.task: Predict all three outputs and explain their different meanings. Repeat the trace for total=0, keeping groups=4.
independent_case.code:
total = 17
groups = 4
print(total / groups, total // groups, total % groups)
independent_case.answer: 4.25, 4 and 1 are ordinary division, whole-number quotient and remainder. At total=0: 0.0, 0 and 0. Groups remains nonzero.

misconceptions: Quotes make a string, even when every character is a digit.
Changing one scalar name updates every earlier assignment
Trace the value bound at each assignment; no formula link is stored.
The right type guarantees valid data
A negative integer can be an invalid object count.
Lowercase false is Python’s Boolean false value
The literal is False; lowercase false is a name and is undefined in a fresh script.

blocks.text: type(count) produces the type of the value bound to count. These print lines display <class 'int'> and <class 'str'>. The quotes in "08" mark text; they are not displayed by print(shelf). True and False have capital initials and no quotes. "False" is text, not a Boolean.
